standard_prerequisites.name: The simple module and its endomorphism skew field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, for a chosen simple module, that its endomorphism ring is a skew field with the same center acting on the module, that the algebra is the endomorphism ring of the module over that skew field, and the dimension formula used at the end.

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicity of a tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the tensor product of the subalgebra with the opposite of the endomorphism skew field is simple, which makes the centralizer simple by the same lemma on simple modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: Matrix algebras over a skew field
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-matrix-algebras and Lemma lemma-simple-module-unique (4)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the description of the tensor product as a matrix algebra over a skew field, and of the module as a direct sum of copies of the simple module of that matrix algebra.

core_obligations: Part (1) and the setup (proof lines 756-768): choosing a simple module and writing the algebra as the endomorphism ring of that module over its endomorphism skew field, the author identifies the module as a module over the tensor product of the subalgebra with the opposite of that skew field and the centralizer as the endomorphism ring of the module over that tensor product, which is simple by the cited simplicity result.

Part (2) (proof lines 770-780): writing the tensor product as a matrix algebra over a skew field and the module as a direct sum of copies of its simple module, four displayed dimension formulas are obtained, from which the identity relating the degrees of the algebra, the subalgebra and the centralizer follows by cancellation.

Part (3) (proof lines 781): applying part (2) to the inclusion of the centralizer and using the obvious containment of the subalgebra in its double centralizer gives equality of degrees and hence equality of the two algebras.
proof_roadmap: Describe the algebra and the subalgebra through a simple module and its endomorphism skew field.
Realise the centralizer as an endomorphism ring over a simple tensor product algebra to get simplicity.
Compare dimensions to get the degree formula, then apply it to the centralizer to get the double centralizer statement.
difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the centralizer of a simple subalgebra of a finite central simple algebra: it is simple, its degree multiplies the degree of the subalgebra to give the degree of the algebra, and it has the subalgebra as its own centralizer (statement lines 745-754). The proof is a complete argument: a simple module and its endomorphism skew field express the algebra, the subalgebra and the centralizer as endomorphism rings of suitable tensor product algebras (proof lines 756-768), simplicity of the tensor product algebra gives simplicity of the centralizer, and the description as matrix algebras over a skew field yields the displayed dimension formulas from which the degree identity is read off (proof lines 770-780); the double centralizer statement follows by applying the same identity to the centralizer (proof line 781). The non-formal content is the identification of the centralizer with an endomorphism ring and the dimension bookkeeping. The claim is H2.
